war_development.label: War Development
war_development.instruction: Roll 1D6 at the start of each Operation.

entries.text: A sector your side controlled has fallen. The front has moved. Command's maps are wrong.
A key figure - a commander, a conduit, an elder - was killed before the mission could begin. Someone else gave the orders you're running on.
A temporary alliance is holding, barely. One of the factions you've fought before is fighting beside you now. Nobody trusts this.
A world your side needed is gone - not taken, destroyed. Scorched, consumed, or silenced. The objective hasn't changed. The reason for it has.
Your side won something. A position, a cache, a system. It cost more than anyone will say. The squad who did it isn't coming back.
Nothing has changed. The front is exactly where it was. All those dead, and the line didn't move.

origin.label: Origin
origin.instruction: Roll 1D6 at campaign start. Select your faction's table.

entries.text: Survivors of a regiment that was officially classified as destroyed six months ago. They kept fighting anyway.
Selected from active service with no explanation given, no request made. They were simply told to report.
A squad that completed a mission Command has since disavowed. They know what they did. So does Command.
A training cohort whose graduation was interrupted by a breach. They've been operational since.
Former rivals from competing Praxium doctrines, forced into a single unit after their respective formations were consolidated.
A squad reconstituted from injury rosters. Everyone here was supposed to be recovering.
A pod split from the main mass during a failed planetary assault. The hive knows they exist. It has not recalled them.
Survivors of a brood-node that was destroyed. The instinct that held them together is older than the node was.
A hunting pattern that developed outside the main consumption wave, moving ahead of the swarm like a shadow it hasn't noticed yet.
A cluster that failed to devour a target and was not reabsorbed. They have been running the same directive ever since.
A pack bred for a specific kill that was never confirmed. The prey may already be dead. They continue regardless.
The remnant of a mass assault that consumed everything it was sent for and then kept going. There were no further orders.
A choir cell that went silent to its own hierarchy six months ago. They operate on doctrine, not instruction.
Missionaries who arrived on a world that was already turning. What they found there changed their doctrine.
A cell built around a relic that has since stopped resonating. They carry it anyway.
Converts from another faction - recent enough that some of them still remember who they were.
The survivors of a ritual that succeeded beyond what anyone intended. The hierarchy doesn't know what to do with them.
A cell that was sent to observe and report. At some point they stopped reporting.
Scouts from the advance wave who returned to find the fleet had not followed. They kept moving.
Exiles from an exile colony - people who were already cast out once and were cast out again.
A warband assembled from two clans who were blood enemies before a common loss made cooperation necessary.
The remnant of a reclamation team that arrived to find the world already gone. They never went home.
Volunteers who left the fleet without authorization. The fleet didn't come after them.
A squad built around a single veteran who remembers the world they're trying to reclaim. Everyone else is going on her word.
Wardens who predate the empire that sent them. The orders they follow are older than the faction that wrote them.
A court in miniature - ancient rivals bound together by a compact that none of them agreed to willingly.
The last functional unit from a domain that no longer exists. They do not yet know this.
Revenants who were dormant for an era and woke to find the world they were guarding had become something else entirely.
A unit whose Prime was destroyed before they could be given purpose. They have been selecting their own objectives ever since.
Wardens bound to a bloodline. The last heir is twelve years old and currently on the front line.
A krump crew who survived a battle so loud it made them famous. They've been sent to prove it wasn't luck.
Veterans of three campaigns who are still alive for no reason anyone has satisfactorily explained, including them.
A squad assembled from the survivors of other squads, all of which were destroyed in the same engagement.
A crew built around a champion who has twice refused honorable death. Command is running out of ways to express its dissatisfaction.
Krumpfists sent ahead of a larger force as bait. They were told they were the vanguard.
A crew who won a battle they were not supposed to survive, then were immediately given another one.

mandate.label: Mandate
mandate.instruction: Roll 1D6 at campaign start. Universal across all factions.

entries.text: The orders they were given no longer reflect the situation on the ground. They haven't received new ones.
They were told to hold something until relief arrived. Relief is not coming.
They are searching for someone. The search has continued long enough that some of them have forgotten why it started.
There is an object, a location, a signal. They cannot confirm it still exists. They cannot stop looking.
They were sent to stop something. They have not confirmed whether they succeeded.
No one alive gave them this mission. They inherited it from someone who didn't make it back.

burden.label: Burden
burden.instruction: Roll 1D6 at campaign start. Universal across all factions.

entries.text: A name. Someone who didn't make it. No one has said why they're still using the callsign.
A piece of intelligence they haven't been able to deliver. The window for it may have already closed.
A promise made to someone outside the squad. The kind that seemed smaller when they made it.
An action from a previous operation that was necessary and has not been discussed since.
A member who should have been rotated out and wasn't. They aren't performing poorly. That's the problem.
The knowledge of where they are on someone else's list. They know they are being used as a disposable asset. They keep going anyway.
